editions.label: Tuesday, 17 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked.

stories.title: NSW pauses a new underquoting rule hours before it was due to start
stories.summary: Premier Chris Minns has put the next part of NSW’s underquoting reforms on hold for up to a year. The rule would have stopped agents advertising below a written offer the seller had already rejected, even if the seller later decided to lower the asking price.
stories.detail: The government says that could make it harder to respond to falling prices. Existing underquoting rules still apply, so the pause is not a licence to advertise below the agent’s genuine estimate.

stories.title: Sydney Airport records 104 cancellations after wind and cloud disrupt flights
stories.summary: Sydney Airport recorded 104 cancellations on Monday, mostly on domestic routes, after wind and cloud reduced air traffic capacity. Qantas said the resulting ground delay programme affected all airlines and it was looking to use larger aircraft on some services to help clear the backlog.
stories.detail: That is Monday’s total, not a forecast for Tuesday. If you are travelling today, check the airline’s flight status before leaving for the airport, especially if a domestic leg is your connection.

stories.title: New records reveal 483 sexual harassment reports against NSW Police employees
stories.summary: Documents obtained by ABC’s 7.30 show 483 reports of sexual harassment against NSW Police employees from 2021 to 2025. The records also list 67 allegations of sexual touching and 10 of indecent assault over the same period.
stories.detail: These are reports and allegations, not findings of guilt or a measure of how many incidents went unreported. The figures add a sense of scale to the workplace culture issues raised in the investigation.

stories.title: Apple News+ puzzles arrive in the Australian iOS 27.3 beta
stories.summary: The second iOS 27.3 beta brings Apple News+ puzzles to Australian subscribers, including a quick crossword, Crossword Mini, Sudoku, Quartiles and Emoji Game. MacRumors found them under Following, then Puzzles, in the News app.
stories.detail: This is a beta release, not a change on the current public build. MacRumors expects the public update in December, so there is no need to install a beta just to get the puzzles early.

stories.title: Tesla plans a €3 billion Cybercab factory expansion near Berlin
stories.summary: Tesla told Reuters it plans a new hall at its Grünheide factory capable of making up to one million Cybercabs a year. It intends to apply for a building permit by year-end, start construction in the first half of 2027 and begin production in 2029.
stories.detail: Those are targets, not output commitments or approval to run Robotaxis on European roads. The Berlin plan is separate from the recent US buyer invitations and does not confirm any change for Australian customers or existing Model Y owners.

stories.title: OpenAI adds more than 20 plugins to ChatGPT for Healthcare
stories.summary: OpenAI says the new plugins are available in ChatGPT for Healthcare, alongside updated clinical search and work on agents that can help with multi-step administrative tasks. It cites organisations using agents for jobs such as processing referrals and moving documents between systems.
stories.detail: This is for governed healthcare workspaces; the separate free clinician offer is for eligible verified US clinicians. The transferable idea for customer success is to test one handoff with synthetic records, allowing the tool to prepare a draft while keeping approval and sending with a person.

stories.title: OpenAI and LVMH’s media division strike a newsroom and content deal
stories.summary: The agreement covers titles including Le Parisien and Les Echos. Staff will be able to explore jobs such as comparing documents and drafting translations. It also calls for ChatGPT to show attributed summaries and excerpts from the publications, with links to the original articles.
stories.detail: Neither partner has given a date for the content changes to reach Australian users. The practical point for research is that the link matters as much as the summary: use the original article to check a quote or figure before reusing it.

stories.title: Coles investigates cyber incident, with no evidence so far of data loss
stories.summary: Coles says it has found no evidence so far that customer, staff or supplier data was compromised or removed. Stores and online shopping continued to operate. Coles was also looking into a small number of Liquorland click-and-collect issues; it had not confirmed those were linked.
stories.detail: Coles says shoppers do not need to act at this point. If a message about the incident asks you to sign in or share information, use the retailer’s app or website directly instead of following the message link.

stories.title: Ukraine holds fresh talks with US and European officials
stories.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine held a new round of online talks with US envoys and European representatives, and participants agreed to meet in Berlin with countries supporting Ukraine. The new element is the direct European participation and planned follow-up, not an agreement with Russia.
stories.detail: The Kremlin says it has not agreed to Europeans joining the next round involving Russian negotiators. There is no confirmed ceasefire or deal, and the format of any further talks with Moscow remains unsettled.

stories.title: Yemen’s pro-government forces pull back to defend Aden
stories.summary: Saudi-backed pro-government forces have withdrawn from parts of western Yemen as Houthi forces advance. The Southern Armed Forces said its priority was defending Aden, the port city where Yemen’s internationally recognised government operates, and neighbouring provinces.
stories.detail: The withdrawal marks a shift in the conflict around the southern Red Sea, a major shipping route. It does not establish that Aden has fallen or that the route has closed.

editions.label: Monday, 16 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked.

stories.title: Researcher warns Western Sydney Airport could add to summer heat
stories.summary: A Western Sydney University researcher says the new airport’s large paved footprint at Badgerys Creek could absorb heat and release it back into the surrounding area. He also raised the possibility that the site could interrupt cooling southerly winds that sometimes bring relief to Penrith.
stories.detail: The airport says it assessed climate risks throughout design and construction and took steps to protect operations during extreme heat. That addresses the airport’s own resilience; the effect on temperatures in neighbouring suburbs has not yet been measured in the reporting.

stories.title: Oberon Council agrees to spend $75,000 after sewage spill
stories.summary: Oberon Council has entered an enforceable agreement with the NSW Environment Protection Authority after untreated sewage escaped from a pumping station into the Fish River over nine days in September 2025. The agreement, rather than a new spill or an ordinary fine, is the development reported this morning.
stories.detail: The Central West council will spend $60,000 over three years removing willows and planting native species along the river, plus $15,000 towards the EPA investigation. The mayor apologised and attributed the discharge to a pump fault.

stories.title: Report: Apple’s smart glasses would rely on Siri and iPhone apps
stories.summary: The latest Bloomberg reporting, covered by 9to5Mac, says Apple wants Siri to control features in third-party iPhone apps through its first smart glasses. The new detail is how Apple expects that to work: the apps would run on the paired phone rather than on the glasses themselves.
stories.detail: A reveal at WWDC in June 2027 and a release later that year are reported targets, not confirmed dates. Apple has not announced the glasses, a price or Australian availability.

stories.title: Tesla lists more range for the base US Model Y, but the EPA listing still differs
stories.summary: Tesla’s US order page now lists 348 miles, about 560 km, for the entry Model Y RWD, up from 321 miles with no change to its US starting price. In a fresh check on Sunday, Drive Tesla found the US government’s fuel-economy database still listed 321 miles for the 2026 Standard RWD with 18-inch wheels.
stories.detail: Tesla has not explained what changed or said the figure applies to cars already delivered. It is a US listing, not a new Australian range rating or an update for existing Model Y owners here.

stories.title: Meituan releases an update to its downloadable talking-avatar model
stories.summary: Meituan has published LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 with downloadable weights under the MIT licence. It turns spoken audio into character animation, and the team reports improved lip sync and more consistent motion on long clips, including videos beyond ten minutes.
stories.detail: This is a model release for teams with suitable compute, not a ready-to-use presentation app. A small, low-risk test would be a clearly labelled training clip with a fictional avatar and a consented voice, then checking whether the extra production work beats recording the same explanation normally.

stories.title: SpaceX recovers Starship’s upper stage after a full orbital test
stories.summary: SpaceX’s launch tower caught the Starship upper stage after it spent more than 22 hours in orbit and deployed 26 Starlink satellites. The Super Heavy booster did not complete its planned return, so the flight did not achieve the intended double catch.
stories.detail: The upper-stage recovery is still a milestone: it demonstrates one of the steps needed to reuse the whole rocket, rather than just its booster. It does not establish how quickly the vehicle can be inspected and flown again.

stories.title: Unions and manufacturers urge the Senate to pass gas reservation
stories.summary: Unions and industry bodies have jointly urged senators to pass the proposed domestic gas reservation scheme as debate gets under way. It would require major exporters to reserve up to 20 per cent of their supply for Australia, with the aim of easing pressure on local gas prices.
stories.detail: The joint push comes from organisations that do not often line up together, including the Australian Workers’ Union and Australian Industry Group. The bill has not passed, and the proposal does not translate into an immediate change to household bills.

stories.title: Israel reports killing Hamas commander as Bahrain says it intercepted attacks
stories.summary: Israel said it killed a senior Hamas military commander in southern Gaza on Sunday. Separately, Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, while Iran claimed it had hit a US military installation in Bahrain.
stories.detail: The US military had not immediately commented on the latest Iranian claim in ABC’s reporting. Bahrain’s account confirms a response to incoming attacks, not that the claimed US target was hit.

stories.title: US flight disruptions carry into a third day, though cancellations ease
stories.summary: US airlines cancelled more than 1,600 flights and delayed almost 3,600 by Reuters’ Sunday update, down from more than 6,400 cancellations on Saturday. US Transport Secretary Sean Duffy expects schedules to be largely normal by Monday US time, but that is a forecast rather than a guarantee for individual flights.
stories.detail: For an Australia-to-US itinerary, the main thing to check is whether a domestic connection is still operating. Delays have persisted after the national ground stop ended, even when long-haul flights are departing.

afternoon.note: New developments since this morning. Times are Sydney local unless noted.

stories.title: Lunchtime hailstorm blankets Mudgee
stories.summary: A lunchtime storm left thick drifts of hail around Mudgee, with residents reporting water entering homes and fallen trees. The NSW SES said it had responded to 18 storm-related incidents across the region, most involving leaking roofs.
stories.detail: At the time of ABC's report, a severe thunderstorm warning covered much of north-east NSW, with large to giant hail and damaging to locally destructive winds possible. Check current warnings before travelling because conditions can change.

stories.title: Apple opens a study of AI answers to health questions
stories.summary: Apple has launched a research app with clinical AI company OpenEvidence to study how people understand and use answers to health questions. Participants can see links to medical research and choose whether to share health data for more relevant responses.
stories.detail: The study is open to up to 200,000 eligible US adults aged 21 or over with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone 15 Pro or later running iOS 26 or later. It is not available in Australia, and Apple says the app is not a substitute for a clinician or intended to diagnose or treat conditions. Study data will not be used to train AI models, according to Apple.
stories.published: 16 Nov, US announcement reported at 12:30 pm Sydney time

stories.title: Helen Haines leaves hospital after alleged attack
stories.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines has been discharged from hospital, four weeks after she was seriously injured outside her electorate office in Wangaratta. The member for Indi lost both legs after being struck by a vehicle.
stories.detail: The Alfred hospital confirmed her discharge on Monday. A 43-year-old man has been charged over the alleged attack.

editions.label: Sunday, 15 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked.

stories.title: Ahmed Al Ahmed speaks about the lasting impact of the Bondi attack
stories.summary: In a new ABC interview, Ahmed Al Ahmed, who helped stop one of the gunmen at Bondi Beach, says he still lives with chronic pain, restricted movement in his arm and disrupted sleep. He returned to Bondi with the ABC and spoke about the toll the attack has taken on his family as well as his health.
stories.detail: The attack is not a new development. The interview is a first-hand account of what recovery has looked like for someone whose actions received worldwide attention at the time.

stories.title: Sydney bus changes start today, including new overnight services
stories.summary: Transport for NSW begins rolling out bus route and timetable changes today, with further changes through December. The package includes round-the-clock service on routes 370 and 343, longer operating hours on several routes serving Bankstown Metro connections, and a new weekday express between Wilton and Campbelltown.
stories.detail: The change is staggered, so not every route moves to its new timetable today. If you are crossing Sydney, use the Trip Planner for the actual day you are travelling rather than relying on an old timetable or familiar interchange stop.

stories.title: Sydney’s housing slowdown is showing up in new lending
stories.summary: ABC analysis published yesterday reports that Sydney and Melbourne have had sharper price falls than the national market. The new lending figures it cites show a 15 per cent fall in new home loans nationally between June and September, with a much steeper 31 per cent drop for investors.
stories.detail: The numbers are national, not an estimate for individual Sydney suburbs. They show that fewer buyers are taking out loans, especially investors, but a cheaper asking price does not necessarily mean a cheaper mortgage while rates remain high.

stories.title: Tesla’s Cybercab order terms rule out commercial use by default
stories.summary: The fine print now reported on Tesla’s personal Cybercab offer rules out listing the car on Tesla’s Robotaxi network or using it for paid rides or deliveries unless Tesla specifically authorises or enables it. That is a material limit on the earlier pitch that owners could earn money from a Cybercab when they were not using it.
stories.detail: Elon Musk also said the required US$299 monthly subscription should be closer to US$115 and that broader US sales depend on regulatory approval. Neither is a confirmed price or rollout change, and there is still no Australian or Model Y announcement.

stories.title: Microsoft says it has restored service to the remaining affected customers
stories.summary: Microsoft now says it has fixed the underlying problem and restored service in the remaining affected regions. That is a step beyond the partial recovery reported yesterday for Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 tools.
stories.detail: Restored access does not resolve every missed appointment, overdue reply or failed integration from the outage. If you are following up with a customer who uses Microsoft 365, check whether the original message or invite landed before sending a duplicate.

stories.title: US links airport disruption to a network upgrade as flight backlog persists
stories.summary: US officials now say work to replace ageing copper cabling with fibre preceded the air traffic communications fault that grounded departures. They are still investigating the root cause, including whether equipment was at fault. The ground stop has been lifted, but airlines are still clearing the backlog of delayed and cancelled flights.
stories.detail: If you are heading to the US, check the onward connection as well as the flight out of Australia. Even when the long-haul service is operating, aircraft and crews can still be out of position on the domestic leg.

stories.title: Zelenskyy says US negotiators raised NATO membership in peace talks
stories.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from Donbas in exchange for NATO membership. This is a newly disclosed idea discussed in talks, not a formal NATO offer or an agreed peace deal. He reiterated that Kyiv is not prepared to give up territory.
stories.detail: Zelenskyy said a comprehensive deal with security guarantees, a well-funded military and reconstruction support could go to a national referendum. The disclosure adds to what is known about the negotiations but does not change the terms of the prisoner exchange already reported.

stories.title: The Philippines wins the first Eurovision Asia contest
stories.summary: Carmelle Allyza San Juan Collado won for the Philippines at the inaugural Eurovision Asia final in Bangkok, performing the original song Sobra-Sobra. The 19-year-old was the youngest contestant in a field representing 11 countries.
stories.detail: China, India and Japan did not take part in the first edition, so the contest’s debut drew a more limited field than its name might suggest.

afternoon.note: Afternoon developments checked in Sydney local time. Quiet categories are omitted.

stories.title: Storm risk extends across NSW this afternoon
stories.summary: The Bureau of Meteorology says severe thunderstorms are likely across parts of eastern Australia today, including areas west of Sydney and north towards south-east Queensland. Damaging winds, large hail and heavy rain are possible, with the highest-risk storms forecast further north.
stories.detail: The bureau's 2 pm forecast for Sydney's outer west warns of possible severe storms and flash flooding this afternoon or early evening. Conditions can change quickly, so check current warnings before heading out.

stories.title: Australia and the Philippines sign defence agreement
stories.summary: Australia and the Philippines have signed the defence cooperation arrangement previewed yesterday. Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro says it will reduce administrative hurdles for joint military activities and disaster response.
stories.detail: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese witnessed the signing in Manila and says the agreement will strengthen maritime awareness, information sharing and training. It comes amid continuing tensions over competing claims in the South China Sea.

editions.label: Saturday, 14 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked.

stories.title: First homes built from NSW’s $1 plans are nearly finished
stories.summary: Four row homes in Corrimal, north of Wollongong, are on track to be the first completed under the NSW Pattern Book scheme. Their builder says approval took eight weeks, compared with the roughly 12 months he would have expected through the usual route.
stories.detail: The $1 was an introductory price for the design, not the cost of building or even the current price of the plans, which is $1,000. More than 25,000 plans have been bought, but only 22 projects are under construction, so this is an early test of whether the scheme can deliver housing at scale.

stories.title: Court clears the way for Newcastle Harbour climate protest
stories.summary: The NSW Supreme Court rejected a bid by NSW Police to stop Rising Tide’s protest on Newcastle Harbour, allowing this morning’s planned event to go ahead. Police raised safety concerns about sharing the water with other harbour users; organisers told the court that life jackets would be mandatory and swimming in the channel would be banned.
stories.detail: The court ruling concerns the event on the water. Newcastle councillors separately voted this week to oppose Rising Tide using council community land for its protests.

stories.title: Apple opens pre-orders for its first LG smart home accessories
stories.summary: The first Apple Home Collection products are now up for pre-order on Apple’s US store: an indoor camera, an outdoor camera and a wired video doorbell, with shipping expected in mid-December. The smart lock and thermostats are listed but not yet available to order there.
stories.detail: The accessories pair by tapping an iPhone and are managed in Apple Home without a separate app or account. Apple lists the US, Canada and the UK for the collection’s initial release, not Australia. That is separate from HomeView, which is already available here.

stories.title: Reported Tesla and SpaceX merger talks draw scrutiny in Texas
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that merger talks have progressed and that a deal could be announced as early as December. Texas attorney-general-elect Nathan Johnson subsequently warned that any deal would face close scrutiny. That is a warning, not an opened investigation or a decision to block a deal.
stories.detail: Tesla has confirmed that an independent board committee is exploring a closer relationship with SpaceX, but neither company has announced a merger. There is no confirmed change for Australian operations or Model Y owners.
stories.published: 13 Nov, 7:22 am; Texas response reported 14 Nov Sydney time

stories.title: Google rolls out the faster Gemini 4 Hydrogen model
stories.summary: Google has begun rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen globally across the Gemini app, Search and developer tools. It is designed for everyday tasks and workflows that use multiple tools, and Google says it completed tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash in its own testing.
stories.detail: Free Gemini users can get Hydrogen through automatic model selection rather than choosing it every time. For a work trial, use an approved workspace and a sanitised set of meeting notes: ask for an action table with one supporting quote per row, then check whether it leaves unassigned actions blank rather than inventing owners.

stories.title: Microsoft reports broad recovery and identifies the outage trigger
stories.summary: Since yesterday’s Australian priority recovery update, Microsoft has apologised and says Outlook and other services are broadly stable again, although full restoration was still in progress at the latest report. It attributed the disruption to elevated load after a network capacity upgrade and said it was not a cyberattack or related to AI agents.
stories.detail: If you are catching up on work, check the delivery status of time-sensitive messages before sending them again. Broad recovery does not mean every mailbox or delayed message has caught up.

stories.title: Split US trade vote leaves Australian lamb tariffs up to Trump
stories.summary: US trade commissioners tied on whether lamb imports had harmed American producers, leaving Donald Trump to decide whether to impose new tariffs or other restrictions. No extra tariff has been announced. Australian lamb already faces a 12.5 per cent US tariff, and Australia exported more than 100,000 tonnes of lamb there last year.
stories.detail: A public hearing on potential measures is set for 1 December, with the commission due to report to Trump by 11 January. Australia argues further restrictions would raise prices for US shoppers.

stories.title: Australia and the Philippines set to sign a defence agreement
stories.summary: Australia and the Philippines are expected to sign a defence cooperation agreement on Sunday, on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila. ABC reports it is expected to expand reciprocal military access and information sharing and support the Philippine Navy and coastguard.
stories.detail: The agreement follows repeated maritime confrontations between the Philippines and China in the South China Sea. The new development is the expected signing, not a deal that has already taken effect.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill three in Zaporizhzhia and Odesa, officials say
stories.summary: Regional officials said three people were killed in Russian strikes on two Ukrainian cities on Friday. A rescue worker died during the response to a hit on an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, where more than 50 people were injured.
stories.detail: Authorities in Odesa said two people were killed and five injured in a strike on a home. The attacks came days after the prisoner exchange agreement reported earlier this week, a limited deal that did not establish a ceasefire.

afternoon.note: Afternoon developments checked in Sydney local time. Quiet categories are omitted.

stories.title: NSW Labor promises 100 public childcare centres if re-elected
stories.summary: NSW Labor has pledged to open and operate 100 long-day childcare centres if it wins the March election. The government estimates they would provide 5,000 places for about 8,000 families.
stories.detail: The proposed centres would be on public primary school sites in areas with too few childcare places, with many expected in Western Sydney and regional NSW. This is an election promise, and sits alongside the existing preschool building commitment.

stories.title: Newcastle harbour protest ends without arrests
stories.summary: More than 600 people took to the water for the Rising Tide protest today, and NSW Police say no arrests were made. Organisers say hundreds more watched from shore.
stories.detail: The Port of Newcastle ran no shipping movements between 10 am and 2 pm. Rising Tide says it plans a larger on-water event in February, shortly before the state election.

stories.title: Tesla invites selected buyers to order a Cybercab
stories.summary: Tesla has invited selected customers to buy the two-seat Cybercab for personal use, with an estimated US$29,990 price before tax. A US$299 monthly autonomy subscription is required to operate it, and the order deposit is US$1,000 and non-refundable.
stories.detail: Tesla estimates deliveries in December and limits operation to supported service areas. The announcement does not confirm Australian availability or a change for Model Y owners, and this invitation is not a general release.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App, citing Tesla

stories.title: US flights resume after nationwide ground stop
stories.summary: The US aviation regulator has lifted a nationwide departure stop caused by an air traffic communications failure. Flights can resume, but delays and cancellations continue as airlines reposition aircraft and crews.
stories.detail: Qantas is offering eligible passengers booked to or from selected US cities on 13 or 14 November fee-free date changes, credits or refunds, subject to its conditions. Check the airline directly for your flight rather than assuming it has been cancelled.

editions.label: Friday, 13 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked.

stories.title: Sydney opens a national hub to tackle online extremism
stories.summary: A $76 million federal centre opens in Sydney today, bringing the Australian Federal Police and ASIO together to tackle online radicalisation. The government says a priority is reaching young people earlier, before online activity escalates into a threat.
stories.detail: The funding was announced in May, so the new development is the centre opening, not a new funding round or a change to the law. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke says the government remains open to further legislative changes.

stories.title: Extra SES crews help Wauchope clean up after hailstorm
stories.summary: The SES responded to 125 calls after Wednesday’s storms on the Mid North Coast and Northern Rivers, more than 70 of them around Wauchope. Crews from Newcastle joined the clean-up on Thursday after hail blocked gutters, water got into buildings and trees came down.
stories.detail: The Lower Clarence was hit by a separate storm cell. Yamba and Iluka also reported roof damage, and fallen trees slowed traffic on parts of the Pacific Motorway near New Italy during the storm.

stories.title: New Apple TV 4K goes on sale in Australia for A$449
stories.summary: The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K reaches Australian stores today, and 9to5Mac’s first review found the new hands-free Siri microphones useful, but answers about the show currently playing could be unreliable. The new model has an A19 chip, though the reviewer found the speed gain over the third generation relatively modest.
stories.detail: Apple confirms the English-language Siri AI beta is also available in Australia on second- and third-generation Apple TV 4K models, with a compatible iPhone or iPad required for the home owner. The first-generation 4K misses out, but the new remote is sold separately if that is the upgrade you actually want.

stories.title: Tesla’s unsupervised US Robotaxi service goes round the clock
stories.summary: Tesla has extended Robotaxi to 24 hours a day across its unsupervised US markets, including newly added San Antonio. The San Francisco Bay Area is the exception, where rides remain supervised. This is an expansion of service hours, not a rollout to new cities.
stories.detail: Tesla has not confirmed that the entire fleet is using the same software version. The change applies to the US ride service and does not announce a software update, an unsupervised feature for your Model Y or an Australian launch.

stories.title: APRA plans to put AI risks into financial-sector stress tests
stories.summary: Australia’s prudential regulator plans to examine AI-driven risks in next year’s stress testing. Its new outlook flags a practical concern for banks, insurers and super funds: disruption can spread when multiple firms depend on the same technology providers, even if each has its own recovery plan.
stories.detail: For a customer planning session, try asking how an AI-assisted journey would keep running if its AI service were unavailable for a day. For example, agree which customer messages can fall back to pre-approved copy and who decides when to switch. That is a suggested exercise, not an APRA requirement.

stories.title: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigns as CEO
stories.summary: Jensen Huang has stepped down immediately as Nvidia’s chief executive, president and board member. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim CEO. His departure followed a board investigation after reporting that Huang had been targeted by foreign intelligence.
stories.detail: Nvidia says it has no reason to believe company security or trade secrets were compromised. The immediate change is at the top of the company; there is no confirmed change to its chip roadmap or supply commitments in the announcement.

stories.title: Microsoft 365 outage hits Outlook, Teams and SharePoint
stories.summary: Microsoft reported disruption across several Microsoft 365 services this morning. At ABC’s 7:36 am update, the company was rerouting traffic and pausing deployments while it worked to restore access. Affected services included Outlook, Teams and SharePoint.
stories.detail: The outage also affected some connections from Claude and ChatGPT to Microsoft 365. If an AI meeting-prep workflow pulled back nothing this morning, check the calendar or document directly before treating an empty result as confirmation that there is nothing scheduled or shared.

stories.title: Trump says the US does not need a deal with Iran
stories.summary: Donald Trump said the US did not need a deal with Iran and told Vice-President JD Vance to focus on domestic corruption. It is a shift in Washington’s public stance after the earlier argument over conditions for talks, but not confirmation that all diplomatic contacts have ended.
stories.detail: Reuters separately reported that Brent crude rose 3.3 per cent to US$95.82 on Thursday as shipping disruption through the Strait of Hormuz and reports of attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure renewed concern about supply. That is a move in wholesale oil prices, not a forecast for Australian petrol prices.

stories.title: New analysis finds some critical medicines repeatedly run short
stories.summary: An ABC analysis of Therapeutic Goods Administration shortage records since 2015 found some critical medicines have repeatedly been in short supply. Examples include a long-acting penicillin injection and Creon, an enzyme replacement used by some people whose pancreas does not make enough digestive enzymes.
stories.detail: The reporting looks at a pattern over years, not a single new shortage announcement. It highlights why the same medicine can be hard to source more than once even when an earlier shortage was listed as resolved.

afternoon.note: Afternoon developments checked in Sydney local time. Quiet categories are omitted.

stories.title: Police conclude Swans investigation without charges
stories.summary: Victoria Police say four Sydney Swans players will not face criminal charges after an investigation into an alleged sexual assault at a Melbourne hotel in August. Police say there was insufficient evidence to lay charges.
stories.detail: Lawyers for three women say they are continuing civil claims related to the allegations. The Swans say their decision to stand players down for breaching club standards was separate from the police investigation.

stories.title: Australia invokes priority recovery agreement as Microsoft outage persists
stories.summary: The federal government has activated an agreement with Microsoft intended to prioritise recovery of Australian services. ASIO and the Australian Federal Police confirmed they were among the organisations affected, showing the disruption extends to national security agencies.
stories.detail: Microsoft said restored servers had again become unresponsive and was preparing a further fix. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke says Microsoft told him it does not believe the outage was caused by a cyber attack; a full recovery time has not been confirmed.

editions.label: Thursday, 12 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked.

stories.title: David Jones names 19 stores to close, including Macquarie Centre
stories.summary: David Jones’s receiver has confirmed that 19 of its 38 stores will shut. Seven are in NSW, including Macquarie Centre, Parramatta and Hornsby, all relevant if you shop around Epping. This is the first confirmed list since the retailer entered administration.
stories.detail: The affected stores are expected to trade through the peak shopping period. Exact closure dates were not given; the company says stock will either be discounted or moved to other stores.

stories.title: NSW premier and ministers subpoenaed over Town Hall protest
stories.summary: Chris Minns, Police Minister Yasmin Catley, Tourism Minister Steve Kamper and senior police have been subpoenaed in the case against people charged over February’s Sydney Town Hall protest. Defence lawyers want to ask how the policing operation was planned and what role ministers played.
stories.detail: ABC reports the subpoenas seek evidence on 8 March, five days before the NSW election. The defence’s claims of improper interference are allegations, not findings; the ministers’ offices declined to comment because the case is before the court.

stories.title: Centennial Park uses beneficial insects to protect its roses
stories.summary: Centennial Park’s horticulture team is using ladybirds and small parasitic wasps to manage aphids in its historic rose garden. It’s an annual intervention, not a one-off experiment, and ABC reports the current infestation has been particularly heavy.
stories.detail: The garden overlooks Busbys Pond and has about 800 plants across 33 rose varieties. If you’re looking for a small stop on a ride or walk through the park, that’s where to find it.

stories.title: Apple Invites adds polls for guests
stories.summary: The latest Apple Invites update lets hosts add a poll so guests can vote on details such as food or a party theme. There’s also a decorative emoji effect, but the poll is the useful change if you want to settle a choice without a group chat.
stories.detail: Hosts still need iCloud+ to create an event. Guests can RSVP from the invitation link without paying or owning an Apple device; Apple Invites is listed in the Australian App Store.

stories.title: Finland clears Tesla’s supervised driver assistance
stories.summary: Finland’s transport regulator recognised the provisional approval granted by the Netherlands for Tesla Assisted Driving, the European name for FSD (Supervised). Tesla says the Finnish rollout will begin soon, which is distinct from the regulatory permission already in place.
stories.detail: The driver remains responsible. This is a Finnish decision, not EU-wide approval, and it does not establish any new feature or eligibility for your Australian Model Y.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App, citing Traficom and Tesla

stories.title: Musk extends the Cybertruck production timetable
stories.summary: Elon Musk says Tesla will now build Cybertrucks through the end of the US summer in 2027, later than the previously reported June or July shutdown. Not a Tesla App reports the extension gives the Texas line more time to work through existing orders.
stories.detail: It is not a reversal of the decision to end production or a promise that all deposits will turn into deliveries. No change to the cancellation of Australian reservations was announced.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App, citing Elon Musk

stories.title: Gemini Live starts rolling out on Apple CarPlay
stories.summary: Google is rolling out the standalone Gemini Live experience on compatible CarPlay displays globally in supported languages. It can pick up recent conversations from your iPhone and, with connected Workspace apps, help you talk through a calendar or inbox. The rollout announcement does not guarantee it has reached every Australian account yet.
stories.detail: This is a CarPlay feature, not a Tesla infotainment update. If you have access in a compatible car, one idea is to rehearse an executive review while parked using a sanitised brief, then pick up the conversation on your phone.
stories.published: 11 Nov, source date; reported 12 Nov, 4:29 am Sydney time

stories.title: SwitchBot puts a removable battery on its retrofit curtain motor
stories.summary: The new Curtain Track 4 fits existing U-rail curtains and lets you remove the Battery+ module for USB-C charging without taking the motor off the rail. It doesn’t fit curtain rods. A compatible SwitchBot hub is needed to bring it into Apple Home through Matter.
stories.detail: It’s available through the US channels cited by 9to5Mac; Australian pricing and stock were not confirmed. Check the rail and hub requirements before ordering.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia agree to a large prisoner exchange
stories.summary: Negotiators from both sides confirmed a planned prisoner-of-war swap after two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. That is a concrete outcome from the talks covered yesterday, but not a ceasefire or a settlement of the territorial dispute.
stories.detail: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due to meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow, then Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin. A timetable for the exchange was not given in the ABC report.

stories.title: Albanese calls for more Pacific climate support at COP31
stories.summary: At the leaders’ summit in Antalya, Anthony Albanese urged countries to help Pacific nations adapt to climate change, pointing to the Pacific Resilience Facility. The appeal came as climate advocates challenged Australia’s support for new coal and gas projects.
stories.detail: The intervention puts Pacific climate finance alongside the argument over how to cut fossil fuel use. Negotiations are still under way; the speech was a call for action, not a new funding agreement.

stories.title: Spain’s housing crisis triggers its first general strike since 2012
stories.summary: Spanish unions say four million people joined a national strike over housing affordability, as tenants’ groups protested rising rents and evictions. The walkout came less than three weeks before the snap general election on 29 November.
stories.detail: Housing was already shaping the election after parliament rejected measures aimed at limiting rent pressure and curbing evictions. The turnout figure is the unions’ estimate.

stories.title: Teenager critical after falling from train on Harbour Bridge
stories.summary: A 17-year-old boy is in a critical condition after falling onto the tracks on the Sydney Harbour Bridge. Police say he was riding on the outside of the train before the fall and are investigating.
stories.detail: The incident briefly stopped T1 services between Wynyard and North Sydney and also affected the T9 Northern Line. Services were delayed by up to 90 minutes earlier, so check live transport information before travelling.

stories.title: National parks booking data stolen across three states
stories.summary: A breach of booking provider Bookeasy has exposed personal information connected with national parks bookings in Queensland, Victoria and South Australia. Queensland says it does not currently believe financial information was accessed, as payments use a separate system.
stories.detail: Park users should be alert to unexpected messages impersonating park staff. Parks Victoria has temporarily suspended new campsite bookings and changes while it investigates, but says existing bookings remain valid.

stories.title: ASIC takes CBA to court over alleged business banking fees
stories.summary: ASIC has launched civil penalty proceedings against Commonwealth Bank, alleging roughly 42,000 CommBiz business customers were overcharged about $8.5 million between November 2020 and May 2025. The regulator says certain transaction fees were not properly disclosed.
stories.detail: CBA says it self-reported and cooperated with ASIC, but disputes some allegations and expects to defend parts of the case. The allegations have not been decided by the court.

editions.label: Wednesday, 11 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked.

stories.title: Newcastle IVF patients face uncertainty over hospital takeover
stories.summary: Calvary Health Care says it will not allow IVF egg collections at hospitals it acquires from Healthscope, a proposed deal that includes Newcastle Private and Hunter Valley Private. Hunter IVF uses Newcastle Private’s operating theatres, but Calvary does not own the fertility clinic or its embryo lab.
stories.detail: Hunter IVF says it is working with alternative providers to avoid interruptions, but where some time-sensitive procedures would take place is still unclear. The takeover needs a NSW hospital licence and a decision from the competition regulator.

stories.title: NSW approves 1.4 GW wind farm near Hay
stories.summary: The Independent Planning Commission has approved the Baldon Wind Farm in the state’s South West Renewable Energy Zone. The project allows 175 turbines up to 300 metres tall, with conditions on road upgrades, traffic and rehabilitation after substantial community opposition.
stories.detail: Planning approval does not mean 1.4 GW is about to reach the grid. Baldon missed out on the zone’s initial transmission access allocation, so its full generating capacity and its ability to deliver that power are separate questions.

stories.title: Apple TV adds on-screen sign language for selected films
stories.summary: Apple announced that viewers will be able to turn on a synchronised interpreter for Being Heumann and F1: The Movie from Friday, with more titles to follow. The initial options are American and British Sign Language, not Auslan.
stories.detail: The controls appear on supported titles after enabling Sign Language in the TV app settings. The report confirms iPhone, iPad and Mac on version 27.2 or later, plus some other app platforms, but does not establish support for the first-generation Apple TV 4K or a separate Australian rollout.

stories.title: Tesla closes orders for another Cybertruck trim
stories.summary: Tesla has stopped taking US orders for the Premium AWD Cybertruck, leaving the Cyberbeast as the only orderable trim, according to Not a Tesla App. It also increased the Cyberbeast’s listed price by US$7,500 to US$109,990.
stories.detail: This is a new change to the US ordering page during the production wind-down, rather than another announcement of the wind-down itself. Tesla has not said whether Premium AWD orders will reopen, and the change does not affect the Australian Model Y line-up.

stories.title: Claude adds collaborative whiteboards and spreadsheets
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Whiteboards and Sheets in beta on paid plans, while Claude Dashboards becomes generally available as Claude Data. The new tools let teams organise notes into a shared board, edit a spreadsheet together and build reports from connected data. Some Claude Data features, including certified queries and live sharing, are still in beta.
stories.detail: For a customer workshop, try a sanitised whiteboard that groups ideas and turns decisions into actions with owners and dates, then review it before sharing. Team plans have the tools on by default, while Enterprise availability depends on admin settings. Anthropic did not specify a separate Australian launch date.

stories.title: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to more users
stories.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available through Google’s API for paying developers and enterprises, with a rollout to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode and Antigravity. Google positions Carbon for demanding, longer tasks, including analysing documents with charts and tables.
stories.detail: It is a broader paid release, not confirmation of access on lower tiers or immediate availability on every Australian account. Google still positions Argon as the everyday option for most knowledge work.

stories.title: Garmin can alert nearby Waze drivers to a cyclist
stories.summary: Garmin has added an opt-in Waze integration for outdoor rides recorded on compatible Edge computers and watches. When a rider shares their LiveTrack position through Garmin Connect, nearby Waze drivers can see a moving alert. Garmin says personal information is not displayed and sharing is limited to the ride session.
stories.detail: It could be useful on road rides if you have compatible gear and are comfortable sharing your live position. It does not alert drivers using other navigation apps, and the release did not specify a separate Australian rollout date.

stories.title: TSMC approves up to US$1 billion in AI investments
stories.summary: TSMC’s board approved up to US$500 million in Anthropic shares at its IPO price and up to US$500 million in OpenAI preferred stock, Reuters reports. The move would give the chipmaker an ownership stake in two major AI developers as well as exposure through its manufacturing business.
stories.detail: The board approvals are investment limits, not confirmation that the full amounts have changed hands.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia resume US-brokered talks without a breakthrough
stories.summary: Envoys from Ukraine, Russia and the US met in Abu Dhabi for their first such talks since February. They discussed security guarantees and territorial concessions, but the sides remain far apart and no ceasefire was announced.
stories.detail: Kyiv is seeking security guarantees, while Moscow wants to address a broader European security framework first. European representatives met separately with Ukrainian and US officials, underscoring the disagreement over who should be involved in a settlement.

stories.title: COP31 electrification pledge runs into a fossil fuel dispute
stories.summary: Türkiye’s proposal to lift electricity to 35 per cent of global energy use by 2035 is meeting resistance because its draft wording does not require the extra electricity to be clean. Critics say the pledge could prolong fossil fuel use if countries meet it with more coal or gas power.
stories.detail: Australia is separately pushing to double the number of households with rooftop solar to at least 300 million by 2030. Both are proposals, not final summit commitments.

stories.title: NSW to recruit 129 hospital security staff
stories.summary: The NSW government says it will recruit 129 additional security staff across 27 hospitals. The announcement follows an alleged attack on a nurse and a doctor at Concord Hospital, where one staff member suffered a broken wrist.
stories.detail: Police say the patient remains in hospital and the incident is under investigation. Health Minister Ryan Park is considering additional powers for security staff, but has not made a decision.

stories.title: Apple Support Community set to close on 20 November
stories.summary: A notice on Apple's support forums says the community will permanently close on 20 November, and new posts are already disabled. Existing discussions can currently be read and searched, but new questions and replies cannot be submitted.
stories.detail: That removes a long-running source of peer troubleshooting for Apple devices. It is unclear whether the existing archive will remain accessible after closure; 9to5Mac has asked Apple to clarify the scope.

stories.title: Russia reports a fresh drone attack on Leningrad region
stories.summary: The regional governor says Russia shot down 92 drones over the Leningrad region early on Wednesday. Reuters could not independently verify the claim. The region contains major Baltic export ports and the Kirishi oil refinery.
stories.detail: Latvia and Lithuania warned residents to seek shelter from unidentified drones entering their airspace, and NATO air defence fighters were activated. The reports come as Russia and Ukraine hold US-brokered talks, but do not establish any change in the negotiations.
